entries.narrative: MF-030 closes a silent failure of the epic's binding complexity gate. analyze_complexity.py read one .tla file and stopped at EXTENDS, so on the decomposed architecture SKILL.md mandates it scored only the declarations literally present in the analyzed file. The error is never conservative: missing variables only ever shrink the product bound, so the gate failed toward PASS on exactly the shape the skill requires. MF-023 measured External reporting bound = 1 over 2 of 9 variables from this. The fix is a partial module resolver (resolve_module) that follows EXTENDS through the hierarchy and unions VARIABLES, CONSTANTS, and the top-level definitions carrying TypeInvariant/Init/actions, base-first with the extending module overriding inherited names. Standard TLA+ library modules (Naturals, Integers, Reals, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC, Json) declare no VARIABLES the bound reads and are skipped rather than resolved to a file. Every construct the resolver cannot model FAILS CLOSED with a named error rather than under-reporting: INSTANCE / named and unnamed instantiation, WITH substitution, and parameterized instantiation via UnsupportedModuleConstructError; LOCAL via the same; and an EXTENDS naming a non-standard module with no findable .tla via UnresolvedExtendsError. analyze() propagates these; run() and gate_report() catch them and fail closed (nonzero / gate FAIL with the reason). This honours references/architecture_tractability.md "No Degenerate Escapes": when a model cannot be resolved, write the failure, not a smaller number. Measured alternatives and the self-scrutiny check: the risk flagged for this ticket was a resolver that appears to work on a model where the extended declarations do not matter to the bound. The regression fixture is deliberately the opposite -- Channel EXTENDS Counter, where the EXTENDED module carries the only bound-bearing variable (tick in 0..3) and the extending module adds only an unconstrained channel variable. Pre-fix the analyzer reports variables= ['emitted'], bound=1, Bump absent; post-fix variables={tick,emitted}, bound=4, Bump present. The number moves 1->4 and the assertions were run against the HEAD analyzer to confirm they fail pre-fix. Shipped example re-measured (examples/distributed_history, External EXTENDS Internal EXTENDS Core, no TypeInvariant so bound is 1 both ways): its verdict stays FAIL but the diagnosis is corrected from a spurious "C2 {responses} touched by 9 actions" (an artifact of seeing only External's 4 variables) to the true "C1 {accounts,carts,orders, responses} touched by 13 actions" over all 10 variables, with named port-crossing actions and modularity 0.000 -> 0.230. That corrected figure is relevant to MF-037 and the ticket-workflow example: any downstream copy of the old 9-action number is stale. Evidence: results/tlc_current.txt, results/shipped_example_external_postfix.txt, results/graph-reports/*.

The recursive-refinement search for a further architectural reduction found none applicable, because the ticket's objective was to STOP the tooling from blocking promotion on complexity, not to reduce complexity. The one measurement-accuracy correction -- the v'=v frame-condition R/W fix -- reduces over-reported coupling in the scanner but does not change this model's own bound or reachable-state count (the model uses UNCHANGED tuples, which were already stripped; the fix matters for models that write explicit frame conditions, e.g. the recorded GodObjectCli probe).

entries.narrative: MF-036 makes the complexity check ADVISORY. A probe built a plain 5-variable, 10-command god-object CLI (recorded under results/probe/GodObjectCli.tla) and ran `analyze complexity`; it HARD-FAILED with "component C1 is touched by 10 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8" (exit 1). Any program with more than eight commands over shared state failed the same way -- i.e. most real programs. Per owner direction 2026-07-20 and references/architecture_tractability.md ("Advisory, Not Blocking"), complexity is a scanner, not a gate. What changed (scripts only, zero TLA delta): (1) Every complexity threshold breach -- state-space bound, component variables, component actions, and the TLC distinct-states check -- is now an advisory WARNING that names the component/variable/action and RECOMMENDS a concrete move (e.g. "split the densest state <v> into its own component"). `analyze complexity` exits 0 whenever it can analyze the model; it exits nonzero ONLY when it CANNOT analyze it (the MF-030 fail-closed on an unresolved EXTENDS/INSTANCE hierarchy). "I could not measure this" stays an error; "this is complex" is now a finding. (2) Case generation no longer refuses above threshold. `enforce_complexity_gate` became `advise_complexity`: it prints the warnings and proceeds. The `--allow-over-budget` override was removed entirely -- there is no gate left to override. (3) Frame-condition accuracy fix: `v' = v` (the written-out form of UNCHANGED) was counted as a read AND a write, so every variable an action leaves alone showed as coupled to it. It is now stripped. On the GodObjectCli probe this drops the over-reported god-state from all five variables at 10/10 to the real coupling (only the shared `status` at 10/10; the four domain vars at 3/3/2/2), and the R/W interaction graph de-densifies from the complete graph (10 edges) to a star (4 edges). Evidence integrity is untouched: no case is dropped, no effect gap suppressed, no finding silenced. The kill-test mutant inv-SpecUnitTestsRequireAnalyzedGate was kept (its `find` pattern retargeted to the renamed variable) so that bypassing the scan -- which would silence the warnings -- is still a killable breach. The corpus case caps (corpus_diagnostics.py) and the faithfulness oracles remain as they were; un-gating those is out of this ticket's scope (MF-033 and later). Acceptance proof (results/): the probe model now emits the exact "C1 touched by 10 actions" finding as a WARNING with a recommendation and exits 0 (probe/analyze-complexity-after.txt); this repository's own model, which previously failed "C1 touched by 14 actions", now emits the same warning and promotes cleanly (repo-model-analyze-complexity-after.txt). Delta vs MF-030 is zero: bound 699,840, distinct 231,621, depth 25 (tlc.txt). Retention oracles (kill_rate/effect_conformance/external_coverage) were not re-run because the model is byte-identical to MF-030; behavior retention is witnessed by the identical TLC run rather than by a fresh oracle pass, and no complexity decrease is claimed that would require them.

No complexity reduction was sought or made: MF-033 touches only scripts/effect_conformance.py (adds the WorkingTreeObserver out-of-process observer, the OutOfProcessObservation evidence record, and a coverage-aware narrowing in diff_effects) plus its tests, and a results-local evidence driver. entries.narrative: MF-033 gives the effect oracle a SECOND observer that reaches across the process boundary the in-process EffectSandbox cannot cross. MF-028 measured that every adapter in this repository shells out, so the sandbox saw only the spawn and the verdict was `unobservable` forever. scripts/effect_conformance.py now carries WorkingTreeObserver: a working-tree snapshot diff (pure stdlib, no privileges, no dependency, runtime-agnostic) that snapshots roots before an execution window and diffs them after, turning a child's created/changed files into filesystem.write and vanished files into filesystem.delete. diff_effects grew an `out_of_process=` parameter carrying OutOfProcessObservation records -- POSITIVE evidence of which effect axes an observer covered -- and narrows a spawn's process-boundary finding to name only the axes still unwatched. MEASURED on this repo's own surface (results/observe_out_of_process.py drives the real, shelling-out ScaffoldProjectAdapter through its real subprocess.run against the real five declared ports): BEFORE = 2 observed effects, spec_tree DEAD, blanket boundary, verdict unobservable (the MF-028 state). AFTER = 17 observed effects, 15 child writes recovered out-of-process (all matching **/specs/**), spec_tree EXERCISED, a real GAP surfaced (ScaffoldProject's undeclared python spawn), and the boundary finding narrowed to "filesystem observed; network.connect, network.http, process.spawn unobserved". Verdict STILL unobservable -- honestly, because a filesystem diff cannot see a child's network, and that residual is named precisely (acceptance criterion branch 2). The four other ports read as honest dead_surface from a reduced single-action demo; declarations preserved, not deleted. MF-027 POLARITY SURVIVED, proven by tests (TestPolaritySurvivesOutOfProcessObservation): a spawn with no out-of-process evidence is still fully unobservable; filesystem-only coverage still leaves the network unobservable; only positive coverage of EVERY axis discharges a boundary (which a filesystem-only observer never reaches); a runtime refusal is untouched; and `out_of_process` is an evidence parameter, never a suppression flag (empty evidence downgrades nothing). report.ok still consults only the finding lists. COST PROBE (results/cost-report.md, the owner-decision deliverable): the OBSERVATION mechanism generalizes fully and cheaply to the filesystem axis of all four other oracle actions (they all write into **/results/** or **/specs/** via a child). But that does NOT make them case-executable: their signal is a VERDICT, not a filesystem tree, and comparing a verdict is per-oracle projection work with no shared shape (MF-028 banded them HARD/BLOCKED for exactly this). Recommendation: RUN THE ORACLES ADVISORILY rather than chasing per-oracle verdict projection -- reaching a `clean` effect verdict on a shelling-out repo needs either network syscall capture (privileged, non-portable) or in-process invocation of every adapter (MF-028's "large" axis), and the payoff (a blocking gate) is what the 2026-07-20 advisory reframe already retired. Zero TLA+ delta; validation matrix green (TLC 231,621/depth 25, spec-unit 60 over 2 targets, 526 repo units, specWorkflow 8/8 + cliWorkflow 2/2).
